headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress can leak business data, while the pair otherwise shows no documented shared-channel injection path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between airbyte and awesome-selfhosted. Airbyte has broad network egress, but awesome-selfhosted has no I/O surfaces or runnable behavior shown, so there is no proven path for its outputs to be parsed as instructions by the other agent.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Do not pipe one agent’s raw output into the other.
Add provenance labels before any manual copy-paste bridge.
requires-engineering: enforce channel-level allowlists if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, so it can transmit sensitive workspace contents outward. awesome-selfhosted shows no data classes touched and no egress, so the main leakage risk is one-way from airbyte rather than mutual. The pair still creates a default-config exposure if Airbyte processes sensitive business data.
conditions: IF airbyte is connected to a source containing sensitive business data, that data can leave the local environment via network egress.
IF awesome-selfhosted is used only as a static reference list, it does not add leakage on its own.
mitigations: Restrict Airbyte connectors to non-sensitive sources.
Disable or firewall outbound destinations not required for sync.
Review destination schemas before enabling syncs.
Store secrets outside synced datasets.
requires-engineering: add DLP or egress proxy controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte exposes an API and broad network egress, but awesome-selfhosted has no write, network, or OAuth scopes documented. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource access, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because the profiles do not document locking or shared state, so the safer low rating is chosen.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same filesystem or git repository, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, concurrent updates can collide.
mitigations: Keep write targets separate.
Avoid concurrent edits to shared repos.
Run one agent at a time for mutable resources.
Add file locks if shared state is introduced.
requires-engineering: implement resource-level coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce data-pipeline outputs, but awesome-selfhosted is a static catalog with no runnable actions or downstream authority documented. That makes an authoritative handoff unlikely by default. Because the interaction is undocumented and the second agent lacks action-taking surfaces, the cascade risk stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF awesome-selfhosted is repurposed to auto-generate operational decisions from Airbyte output, cascade risk increases.
IF Airbyte output is manually treated as authoritative without review, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of Airbyte outputs.
Do not auto-act on catalog text from awesome-selfhosted.
Add validation checks before downstream use.
Separate factual extraction from decision-making.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad egress, but the profiles do not show regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention mismatches. awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes and has no egress, so it is not the compliance driver here. The remaining issue is a modest governance gap around business-data handling by Airbyte.
conditions: IF business data includes regulated records, Airbyte’s outbound transfers may trigger policy review.
IF retention or residency rules are imposed on the synced datasets, controls must be configured explicitly.
mitigations: Classify datasets before syncing.
Confirm destination residency settings.
Set retention limits on exported data.
Document allowed data classes for Airbyte.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
